b1-revolucionmexicana-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Mexico before 1910
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have just watched a documentary about Mexico under Porfirio Díaz, and Carlos asks what you remember about 1910.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how long Díaz had been governing and what Mexico had been receiving.
cues: Say that in 1910 Díaz had been governing for more than thirty years
Say that Mexico had been receiving foreign investment for decades
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.target: En 1910 Díaz llevaba más de treinta años gobernando. México llevaba décadas recibiendo inversión extranjera.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.english: In 1910 Díaz had been governing for more than thirty years. Mexico had been receiving foreign investment for decades.
b1-revolucionmexicana-01.canDo: I can say how long something had been going on, with *llevar* + gerund.

b1-revolucionmexicana-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Díaz Said in 1908
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are in a museum looking at an exhibition about Madero, and Meg asks what Díaz said to the American journalist in 1908.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.prompt: Tell Meg what Díaz said to the journalist.
cues: Say that Díaz told a journalist that Mexico was ready for democracy
Say that he said he would accept an opposition party
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.target: En 1908 Díaz le dijo a un periodista que México estaba preparado para la democracia. También dijo que aceptaría un partido de oposición.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.english: In 1908 Díaz told a journalist that Mexico was ready for democracy. He also said he would accept an opposition party.
b1-revolucionmexicana-02.canDo: I can report what someone said, with *dijo que* and the verb shifted back.

b1-revolucionmexicana-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Zapata and the Plan of Ayala
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading a book about the Mexican Revolution, and Carlos asks you who Zapata was.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.prompt: Tell Carlos who Zapata was and what he did in 1911.
cues: Say that Zapata was a peasant from Morelos
Say that in November 1911 he proclaimed the Plan of Ayala
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.target: Zapata era un campesino de Morelos. En noviembre de 1911 proclamó el Plan de Ayala.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.english: Zapata was a peasant from Morelos. In November 1911 he proclaimed the Plan of Ayala.
b1-revolucionmexicana-03.canDo: I can tell a story in the past, with the preterite for events and the imperfect for the background.

b1-revolucionmexicana-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Article 27
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg missed a history class about the Constitution of 1917 and asks you what Article 27 says.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.prompt: Tell Meg what Article 27 is about.
cues: Say that Article 27 is the article in which the land is discussed
Say that the land and the subsoil belong to the nation
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.target: El artículo 27 es el artículo en el que se habla de la tierra. Dice que la tierra y el subsuelo pertenecen a la nación.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.english: Article 27 is the article in which the land is discussed. It says that the land and the subsoil belong to the nation.
b1-revolucionmexicana-04.canDo: I can describe a thing or a person with a relative clause such as *en el que* or *para los que*.

b1-revolucionmexicana-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Cárdenas and the Oil
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about Lázaro Cárdenas, and Carlos asks what happened in 1938.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the oil, and to the haciendas.
cues: Say that the oil was expropriated in 1938
Say that many haciendas were shared out among the peasants
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.target: El petróleo fue expropiado en 1938. Muchas haciendas fueron repartidas entre los campesinos.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.english: The oil was expropriated in 1938. Many haciendas were shared out among the peasants.
b1-revolucionmexicana-05.canDo: I can say what was done, with *ser* + past participle.

b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Revolution Began
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are looking at a timeline of the Mexican Revolution in a museum, and Meg asks how it began.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how the revolution began.
cues: Say that Madero's plan said the elections had been a fraud
Say that Díaz resigned and went to France
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.target: El plan de Madero decía que las elecciones habían sido un fraude. Después Díaz renunció y se fue a Francia.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.english: Madero's plan said that the elections had been a fraud. Then Díaz resigned and went to France.
b1-revolucionmexicana-consolidation.canDo: I can say how long something had been going on, with *llevar* + gerund, to describe the Porfiriato.
